content.user_title: Route Prompts to a Chosen Claude Model
content.value_statement: Automatic model selection can pick a different model than the user intended. This skill lets users explicitly route a prompt to Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus.
actual_capabilities: Parses the first argument as a requested model alias.
Supports haiku, fast, sonnet, standard, opus, and deep aliases.
Routes requests to fast, standard, or deep executor subagents.
Preserves the remaining user query for the selected executor.
Shows usage help when the model alias is missing or invalid.
Labels the response with the model used.
limitations: It does not choose a model automatically.
It depends on matching executor subagents being available.
It only supports Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus model classes.
It does not estimate cost, latency, or policy impact.

use_cases.title: Control Model Cost
use_cases.description: Route simple requests to Haiku when speed and cost matter more than deep reasoning.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Workflows
use_cases.description: Send normal coding tasks to Sonnet so team members use a consistent default model.

use_cases.title: Force Deep Review
use_cases.description: Route architecture, security, or design reviews to Opus when the task needs deeper analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Route a Quick Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a fast answer.
prompt_templates.prompt: /route haiku Summarize this issue in three direct bullets.

prompt_templates.title: Route a Coding Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Routine development help with the standard model.
prompt_templates.prompt: /route sonnet Review this component and suggest focused improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Route a Deep Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Complex reasoning where the user wants the strongest model.
prompt_templates.prompt: /route opus Analyze this authentication flow for design risks and missing checks.

prompt_templates.title: Use Alias-Based Routing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using shorter model aliases.
prompt_templates.prompt: /route deep Compare these migration options and recommend a rollout plan.

output_examples.input: A user requests Opus for an authentication design review.
output_examples.output: The assistant routes the request to the deep executor and labels the response as Opus.

output_examples.input: A user requests Haiku for a short summary task.
output_examples.output: The assistant routes the request to the fast executor and labels the response as Haiku.

output_examples.input: A user enters an unsupported model name.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns concise usage help with the supported model aliases.

best_practices: Choose Haiku for simple tasks that need fast responses.
Choose Sonnet for routine coding, documentation, and review work.
Choose Opus for complex analysis where accuracy matters more than cost.
anti_patterns: Do not expect the skill to classify task complexity automatically.
Do not use the most capable model for every short request.
Do not use routing instructions to bypass platform safety requirements.

faq.question: Does this skill choose the model automatically?
faq.answer: No. The user must provide a supported model alias as the first argument.

faq.question: Which model aliases are supported?
faq.answer: It supports haiku, fast, sonnet, standard, opus, and deep.

faq.question: What happens after a valid model is selected?
faq.answer: The skill routes the remaining query to the matching executor subagent.

faq.question: Can it route non-coding tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. The routing logic is based on the requested model, not the task topic.

faq.question: Does it reduce token cost by itself?
faq.answer: No. It only routes to the selected model. Cost depends on the chosen model and request size.

faq.question: What should I do when the alias is invalid?
faq.answer: Use one of the documented aliases, then place the full query after the alias.
